title: Lemire half-degree irreducible binary polynomial conjecture
statement: For every integer n >= 1, there exists a monic irreducible polynomial f in GF(2)[x] of degree n such that deg(f - x^n) <= floor(n/2).

provenance.source: Daniel Lemire and Owen Kaser, Strongly universal string hashing is fast, The Computer Journal 57(11), 2014, Section 4.1 and footnote 4, https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4961

notes: The dependencies record the currently selected sufficient proof route, not a claim that the endpoint Möbius-convolution statement is logically necessary. Axeyum has established the finite interval 1 through 400. The exact endpoint reductions, proper-power subtraction, and reciprocity show that the stated signed Möbius-convolution bound for both endpoint degrees at every ell >= 200 would settle all remaining degrees. That aggregate cancellation premise remains unproved, so this fact has no evidence and remains conjectured.
